title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
authors: Gabriele Bellomia, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Massimo Capone, Adriano Amaricci
abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.
summary: This work develops a novel method to analyze entanglement in strongly correlated electron systems by introducing a symmetry resolution to two-site entanglement measures. Applied to the Hubbard model via CDMFT, the technique successfully distinguishes entanglement sources related to spin fluctuations versus charge fluctuations. This provides deeper insight into the distinct quantum mechanisms driving Mott and pseudogap physics.
main_problem: The paper aims to identify and characterize intrinsic quantum resources within strongly interacting fermionic systems, specifically focusing on the physics governing Mott and pseudogap states.
main_result: The introduction of a symmetry resolution to two-site entanglement allows researchers to distinguish contributions from different physical mechanisms, such as spin-singlet fluctuations (Mott insulator) versus holon-doublon correlations (pseudogap metal).
method: The study employs a symmetry resolution technique applied to bipartite entanglement measures, including fermionic negativity and relative entropy of entanglement, within the framework of cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT).
model_or_system: The primary model is the single-band Hubbard model, which is used to simulate strongly correlated electron systems relevant to high-Tc superconductors. Calculations are performed on plaquette clusters using CDMFT at zero temperature.
key_observables: Symmetry-resolved two-site entanglement (decomposed into 0-charge jump, 2-charge jump, and hopping-induced components); fermionic negativity; relative entropy of entanglement.
important_parameters: Interaction strength (U), hopping parameter (t), chemical potential ($\mu$), and doping level (related to filling).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extending entanglement measures to mixed two-site states and assumes that the symmetry resolution can successfully decouple distinct physical contributions to entanglement.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the analysis tracks entanglement evolution across Mott transitions and through the pseudogap regime.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the symmetry-resolved entanglement measure, then applies this measure to the Hubbard model on a dimer, and finally extends the analysis to the full plaquette cluster using CDMFT to track phase transitions.
why_interesting: The methodology of using symmetry-resolved entanglement provides a powerful diagnostic tool to dissect the complex quantum correlations underlying exotic phases like the pseudogap, which is a major topic in strongly correlated physics.

The two-site entanglement Ei j is introduced by the off-diagonal terms, which can be grouped into three symmetry classes. Hopping amplitudes (yellow), antiferromagnetic amplitudes (cyan) and holon-doublon am- plitudes (magenta). White boxes represent zero elements. The Fock basis states are reordered to highlight the respective symmetry blocks in ρi j and ρF i(j)⊺.

Figure 3: Symmetry decomposition of a generic, mixed two-site density matrix ρi j (top panel) and its fermionic partial transpose ρF i(j)⊺(bottom panel), for a Hubbard system. The mixed character of the state populates all the charge symmetry sectors in ρi j. The resulting additional hopping amplitudes break the symmetry decomposition of ρF i(j)⊺, unless they are removed by the parity superselection rule. White boxes represent zero elements. The Fock basis states are reordered as in Fig. 2, to highlight the symmetry blocks in ρi j and ρF i(j)⊺.
Figure 4: Different measures of full and symmetry-resolved entanglement between the two sites constituting an isolated Hubbard dimer, in its half-filled ground state.

Figure 6: Local von Neumann entropy Si [73–78], local electron density 〈ni〉and local nonfreeness I(↑:↓) [41,125–129] across the density-driven Mott transition. All data points pinned at 〈ni〉= 1 (half-filling), represent the incompressible Mott insulator. At intermediate density 0.83 ≲〈ni〉< 1, the system is delocalized into a strongly correlated – meaning large I(↑:↓) – metal, akin to the pseudogap regime of cuprates. Finally, the metal found for 〈ni〉≲0.76 features a full Fermi surface and becomes weakly correlated – meaning vanishing I(↑:↓) – at very low electron density.
